notes: Brackets: the booklet prints one 5.0% rate on 5.0% income (p12 line 22: tax table under 24,000, multiply by 0.05 over 24,000); the same flat schedule is given for every filing status. Short-term gains (8.5%) and collectibles gains (12%) are in capital_gains, not brackets.
Optional voluntary 5.85% rate in place of 5.0% (p12 Line 22 note; p29 Schedule D line 22): not modelled, a filer's election; it does not apply to 8.5% or 12% income.

base.starts_from is state_own: Form 1 builds income line by line (wages, pensions, interest, etc.); federal AGI is only an information item (p9 'Federal Adjusted Gross Income'). Massachusetts conforms to the IRC as of 1 Jan 2024 with listed exceptions (p4).

Standard deduction: not found in the booklet; Form 1 uses exemptions (lines 2a-2f) and the deductions on lines 11-15 and Schedule Y. Recorded the personal, dependent, age 65 and blindness exemptions; medical/dental (line 2e, federal Sch A line 4 amount) and adoption agency fee (line 2f, fees paid) exemptions have no fixed amount and are not recorded.

Base deductions recorded as 'other': FICA/Medicare/Railroad/US-or-MA retirement contributions (max 2,000 per person, line 11, p11), rental deduction (50% of rent, max 4,000 per return, 2,000 if married filing separately, line 14, p12), student loan interest (max 2,500, Sch Y line 10, p22). Many other Schedule Y deductions (alimony paid, HSA, tuition 25%-of-AGI test, charitable, commuter 750, etc.) are not recorded.

Capital gains: long-term gains (other than collectibles) are taxed at 5.0%, same as ordinary (p29 Schedule D line 22), so no entry. Gains on collectibles and pre-1996 installment sales classified as capital gain are 12% (p13 line 23b; p27) with a 50% long-term deduction if held over one year (p27); the Schedule B line 27 worksheet applies it to collectibles gains (p26). Short-term gains are 8.5% (p13 line 23a).
Capital losses: long-term losses can offset interest and dividends only up to 2,000 (p27 worksheet); not held by the schema.

Excess unused exemptions (when exemptions exceed 5.0% income) can be applied against interest, dividends, 8.5%/12% income and then long-term gains, only single, head of household or joint (p12 worksheet); not held by the schema.

Surtax: 4% on taxable income over 1,083,150 for 2025, for residents; for non-residents on the part sourced to Massachusetts (p3, p14). Same threshold stated for every status (no per-status amount printed), so recorded under 'all'.
Surtax measure: booklet says 'taxable income' without defining it further; recorded base 'other' with as_printed text.
Social Security: not taxed ('Massachusetts does not tax Social Security income', p10; excluded from gross income p6).

Pensions: exempt = contributory pensions of the US government or Massachusetts and its political subdivisions (p10), and noncontributory military/uniformed services pensions and survivor benefits (p10-11). Pensions from other states are reported on line 4 and deducted on Schedule Y line 13 under the tests of TIR 95-9 (now in the sources): three entries, one for New York (the only paying state the sources name), one for a state with no income tax, one for any other state with a specific pension exclusion, deduction or exemption that would apply to a Massachusetts pension. Noncontributory public pensions other than military are taxable where the sources address them (pre-1975 state judges, p11; senior U.S. judges, 'not contributory'; ch 32 ss 56-60 veterans after a lump sum, p11). Private pensions: 'Income from most private pensions or annuity plans is taxable in Massachusetts' (p10).

Railroad retirement benefits: not found in the Form 1 instructions as an income kind; the DOR page 'Tax Treatment of Government Pensions' says 'Tier I or Tier II railroad retirement benefits are exempt from Massachusetts taxation' and that 'Social Security benefits' includes Tier I: entry railroad_retirement_exempt.

IRA/Keogh distributions, including qualified charitable IRA distributions and Roth conversions, are taxable to the extent they exceed contributions previously taxed by Massachusetts (Schedule X line 2 worksheet, p20; p11 rollover paragraph); 401(k) rolled into an IRA is generally fully taxable on distribution (p20). Private pensions and annuities are generally taxable (p10). No age-based retirement exclusion found in the booklet.
Firefighter/police line-of-duty incapacity exclusion (Sch Y line 4a, p21) recorded as a subtraction covering wages with no cap stated; the booklet gives no age or amount test.

Circuit breaker credit (age 65+, max 2,820; total income limits 75,000 single, 94,000 head of household, 112,000 joint; property value limit 1,298,000; p3, p8) is a credit on real estate tax or rent, not on an income kind in the schema; not recorded as a relief. No Tax Status and Limited Income Credit thresholds (p13-14) also not recorded: they are not held by the schema.

Indexing: only the surtax threshold, circuit breaker amounts and the section 179 limits are said to be inflation-adjusted. Nothing is said about brackets, exemptions or deductions, so those are not_stated.
Muni interest: interest from other states' obligations is included in gross income; interest on Massachusetts obligations is excluded (p6, p24-25).
Settlement 2026-11-06: married_separate and head_of_household brackets dropped (the booklet prints one rate for all); surtax measure set to state_taxable_income (booklet: 'taxable income').
Format update 2026-11-06: recapture added (none found in the booklet).

Settlement 2026-11-07: other_state_contributory_pension: covers was public_pension; rule 14 asks public_pension_other_state for another state's pension that the state treats differently from its own, and the sources do (TIR 95-9). Split into three entries by TIR 95-9's tests: _ny (paying_states NY, age 59.5, 20,000 a person, Examples 1-2), _no_income_tax (test 3, all of it), and the general entry (tests 1-2, the amount the other state would allow).

Settlement 2026-11-07: TIR 95-9's tests name 'a specific income exclusion' or 'a specific deduction or exemption' for pension income; none of the sources mentions a credit either way, so a paying state's pension credit is not recorded as qualifying or as not qualifying.

Settlement 2026-11-07: TIR 95-9 cites the New York provision as 'Section 617(c)(3-a)'; Letter Ruling 81-91 quotes the same text as 'N.Y. Tax Law, Section 612(c)' paragraph 3-a. Recorded as the TIR prints it in the cite; the figure (20,000 at 59 1/2) is the same in both.

Settlement 2026-11-07: Letter Ruling 81-91 (1981) held a New York State contributory pension fully taxable to a Massachusetts resident because New York's exclusion was not a 'blanket exemption'; TIR 95-9 revokes it ('This TIR revokes Letter Rulings 81-91 and 85-12 and Technical Information Releases 80-4 and 89-10'). Not used for any rule.
Settlement 2026-11-07: railroad_retirement_exempt added from the DOR page 'Tax Treatment of Government Pensions' (Tier I and Tier II exempt; lump-sum insurance and residual payments exempt).
Settlement 2026-11-07: us_ma_contributory_pension not_covered: added senior U.S. judges' pensions (taxable, 'not contributory'; Tax Treatment of Government Pensions).

Settlement 2026-11-07: age_65_exemption kept at 700. The 2025 Form 1's text layer (pypdf and docling) reads 'x $ 1,700 = 2c', but the rendered PDF page 1 prints 'x $ 700 = 2c', matching the instructions (PDF p10 Line 2c, $700); the '1' is a text-layer artifact.

Settlement 2026-11-07: the DOR page 'Differences between MA and federal tax law' says pensions eligible for the exclusion include 'contributory plans of other states' with no reciprocity test; the instructions (p22) and TIR 95-9 state the test, and are followed.

Settlement 2026-11-07: the three new DOR pages are not in fetch.json; their cite.url is the registry address and accessed the date their files were retrieved (2026-11-07 UTC). The pensions page's own canonical address is https://www.mass.gov/info-details/tax-treatment-of-government-pensions.

reliefs.cap_rule: No fixed cap. The deduction 'will equal the amount of the specific pension exclusion, deduction, or exemption that could be claimed by the taxpayer under the laws of the other state if the taxpayer were a resident of the other state and received the income from a Massachusetts state or local contributory pension' (TIR 95-9). Part-year residents: 'If a partial exclusion from income applies, reduce the Massachusetts related exclusion by the amount excluded in the former state during the same tax year.'
